newsitem.title: FINLAND: Merita repeats Nokia holding is long term.
newsitem.headline: Merita repeats Nokia holding is long term.

text.p: Finnish banking group Merita Oy repeated on Friday that its 10.2 million shares in telecoms group Nokia Oy are a long-term holding.
It was commenting on market talk that it may plan to sell the shares in order to return a pension contribution surplus from its pension fund to the banking group.

Merita spokesman Timo Nikinmaa told Reuters the bank did indeed plan to transfer a surplus "in the region" of 1.5 billion markka, principally attributable to gains in Nokia's share price, but this would not require selling any shares.
"It would be an accounting operation," he said.
"We have no plans to sell our Nokia shares. The stake is a long-term investment," Nikinmaa said.
According to Nokia's 1995 annual report, 10.02 million of its shares were owned by Merita's pension fund at end-1995.
Nikinmaa said the book value of the group's Nokia stake was 628 million markka, i.e. about 62 markka per share.
Nokia on Friday traded above 213 markka.
Nikinmaa said the return of surplus contributions would become possible once parliament has passed a tax law to the effect. @
The proposal is currently being debated in parliament committees and it is still possible that the law could be passed this year, Nikinmaa said.
If Merita made the transfer, the extraordinary income would be taxable under the avoir fiscal system at the 28 percent corporate and capital gains tax, he noted.
